questions.stem: According to the pressure-flow hypothesis, what causes the movement of sugars through the phloem?

options.text: Sugars move by diffusion from high to low concentration
A difference in hydrostatic pressure between the source and the sink drives mass flow
The transpiration stream pulls sugars along with water
Root pressure pushes sugars upwards from the roots

questions.explanation: In the pressure-flow hypothesis, sucrose is actively loaded at the source, lowering the water potential and drawing in water by osmosis. This raises the hydrostatic pressure at the source. At the sink, sucrose is removed, so pressure is lower. This pressure difference drives mass flow from source to sink.
